questions.question: Which of the following best describes a common strategy for SQL query tuning to improve performance?
options: Increasing the number of indexes on a table
Utilizing EXPLAIN to analyze query execution plans
Avoiding the use of WHERE clauses to speed up data retrieval
questions.correctAnswer: Utilizing EXPLAIN to analyze query execution plans
questions.explanation: Option C is correct because using EXPLAIN to analyze query execution plans helps identify bottlenecks and optimize SQL queries. Option A is incorrect because nested loops can be inefficient. Option B is incorrect because while indexes can improve performance, adding too many can degrade it. Option D is incorrect because WHERE clauses are essential for filtering data efficiently.

questions.question: In a microservices architecture, what is a recommended practice for inter-service communication?
options: Using direct database calls between services
Storing all service states in a shared database
Employing RESTful APIs or message brokers for communication
Relying solely on synchronous communication methods
questions.correctAnswer: Employing RESTful APIs or message brokers for communication
questions.explanation: Option C is correct because using RESTful APIs or message brokers allows services to communicate independently and asynchronously, promoting loose coupling. Option A is incorrect because direct database calls violate service boundaries. Option B is incorrect because a shared database can create tight coupling. Option D is incorrect because relying solely on synchronous communication can lead to performance issues and bottlenecks.

questions.question: When designing a caching strategy with Redis, which approach is most effective for handling cache invalidation?
options: Never invalidating the cache to avoid overhead
Using a time-to-live (TTL) strategy for automatic expiration
Storing all data in the cache without any expiration
Manually invalidating the cache after every database update
questions.correctAnswer: Using a time-to-live (TTL) strategy for automatic expiration
questions.explanation: Option B is correct because using a TTL strategy automates cache expiration, ensuring data remains fresh without manual intervention. Option A is incorrect because never invalidating the cache can lead to stale data. Option C is incorrect because storing all data without expiration can lead to excessive memory usage. Option D is incorrect because manual invalidation is error-prone and inefficient.

To transform elements in an array
To reduce an array to a single value
